Despite facing a second trade secret theft lawsuit over its hardware business in just over a year, OpenAI still plans to release its first product this year and officially launch it in 2027, according to Bloomberg. Here are the details.

First product still scheduled for unveiling in 2026

Last Friday, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company and several former Apple employees of stealing confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's consumer device business.

The lawsuit detailed a 'pattern of theft of Apple trade secrets' by former OpenAI employees and alleged that 'such misconduct has been normalized and set as an example by leadership.'

This lawsuit adds to the growing legal troubles OpenAI faces over its hardware business, following another lawsuit previously filed by startup iyO. That lawsuit initially focused on branding matters before being amended to add allegations of trade secret misappropriation.

Despite the news last Friday, OpenAI currently appears to be sticking to its hardware roadmap. According to Bloomberg:

Since OpenAI announced its partnership with Jony Ive's io Products to develop an 'AI-first' device, there has been much speculation in the market trying to guess what OpenAI is actually planning.

After the two sides announced their collaboration in May 2025, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo immediately stated that OpenAI's first device would be a small, screenless pendant-style product, equipped with cameras and microphones to capture the user's surroundings, with computing and display functions provided via a smartphone.

OpenAI, for its part, has hinted at plans to launch multiple devices rather than a single product, and stated in court filings related to the iyO lawsuit that its first product would not be an in-ear or wearable device—a departure from what many had speculated when the partnership was first announced.
